t: PEV is fractal (same pattern at every scale) and user attention duration is a measurable alignment metric
description: Three connected insights from Session 102: (1) PEV operates at every scale — lug, advisor, spoke, hub, user. It's not repetition, it's the operating model asserting itself fractally. (2) User attention duration per spoke is a signal — which spoke gets the most time reveals actual priority, which can be compared against Lathe's projected optimal path to produce an alignment score. (3) Hub is the dispatch layer for light directives (tender fans out), spokes are execution, user attention is verification. This means Compass needs session duration tracking per spoke, Lathe needs projected time allocation, and the delta between them is a new first-class metric.
implications: Compass MVP should include attention-vs-plan alignment metric
Session tracks already contain duration — aggregate per spoke at hub level
Lathe shift directions become testable: did actual attention match the plan?
Hub dispatch model is already working (tender) — formalize it

_behavior_directive.what_this_is: Architectural signal: PEV is the unified operating model at every scale. Attention tracking closes the verification loop at the user level.
_behavior_directive.what_this_is_NOT: Not a task to implement. This is a design signal that should influence Compass, Lathe, and hub dispatch design.
